app: GNOME Text Editor — hard-text stress (ligatures, accents, RTL Arabic, emoji, CJK)

stack_detection.signature: libgtk-4.so; text nodes name their font per run

channel_setup: GSK render tree via gdb tap; per-text-node glyph IDs decoded with the node's OWN named font (reverse cmap) + Unicode NFKC + BiDi reorder.

t1_read_text.detail: All runs recovered when decoded with the correct per-node font (the tree names it, and font fallback splits runs by font): Latin 'office finance flag' ✓; precomposed accents 'café','naïve' ✓ (glyphs 171→é, 177→ï); CJK '你好' ✓ (WenQuanYi font); emoji '😀' ✓ (Noto Color Emoji, single color glyph 883). RTL Arabic recovered as presentation forms in visual order (ﺎﺒﺣﺮﻣ), then NFKC → base letters and reverse → 'مرحبا' exactly. Ligatures decompose via NFKC (ﬁ→fi, ﬂ→fl).

measurements.notes: Stronger than predicted. The 'glyph problem' is largely solved by three cheap steps: (1) use the per-run font the tree already names (fallback splits runs, so emoji/CJK land in their own nodes with the right font); (2) reverse cmap; (3) Unicode NFKC + BiDi reorder for presentation-form scripts and standard ligatures. Residual lossy cases: discretionary/custom ligatures with no NFKC decomposition (need GSUB reversal) and complex mixed-direction BiDi runs (need the run's resolved levels). These are a small, characterizable tail — and are DETECTABLE (a glyph with no cmap entry is a known miss), so they degrade explicitly, not silently.

runtime_verification.method: decoded strings compared to the known source file contents
runtime_verification.agreement: exact for Latin/accents/CJK/emoji; exact for Arabic after NFKC+reorder
